questions.stem: A person who travels to Calabar from Kaduna, stays five nights for the carnival and returns home is best described as a
questions.explanation: A tourist stays away from home at least one night and less than a year.

questions.stem: A visitor who travels from Abeokuta to Ibadan to see a museum and returns home the same day is called an
questions.explanation: Same-day visitors who do not stay overnight are excursionists.

questions.stem: A student is listing the industries that make up tourism. Which group should she include?
options: Crude oil refining and the sale of petroleum products
Accommodation, transport, attractions and travel trade
questions.explanation: Tourism covers hospitality, transport, attractions and travel services.

questions.stem: Hotels, restaurants and bars that provide food, drink and lodging to visitors make up the
questions.explanation: Hospitality is a core part of tourism.

questions.stem: The Englishman credited with organising the first package excursion by rail in 1841 is
questions.explanation: Thomas Cook arranged a rail excursion in 1841, pioneering package tours.

questions.stem: Which development in the twentieth century did most to make long-distance mass tourism possible?
options: Growth of commercial jet air travel
Building of canals for barges carrying passengers between towns
questions.explanation: Jet aircraft cut travel time and cost, enabling mass tourism.

questions.stem: A Nigerian family on holiday at Obudu Mountain Resort in Cross River State is engaged in
questions.explanation: Travel within one's own country is domestic tourism.

questions.stem: Visitors who travel to Yankari to watch wildlife in its natural habitat while supporting conservation are engaged in
questions.explanation: Nature-based, conservation-friendly travel is eco-tourism.

questions.stem: The three main components of tourism, often called the three As, are attraction, accessibility and
questions.explanation: Attraction, accessibility and amenities.

questions.stem: Good roads, airports and transport links to a tourist site are examples of
questions.explanation: Accessibility is the ease of reaching the destination.

questions.stem: A hotel room not sold tonight cannot be stored and sold tomorrow. This shows that the tourist product is
questions.explanation: Unsold capacity is lost: tourism products are perishable.

questions.stem: Tourists must travel to Olumo Rock to enjoy it, since it cannot be brought to them. This characteristic of the tourist product is
questions.explanation: Tourist attractions are immovable; consumers come to them.

questions.stem: Olumo Rock, a well-known tourist attraction, is located in
questions.explanation: Olumo Rock is in Abeokuta.

questions.stem: The Ikogosi Warm Springs, where warm and cold springs meet, are found in
questions.explanation: Ikogosi is in Ekiti State.

questions.stem: The number of foreign visitors entering a country in a year is recorded in tourism statistics as
questions.explanation: Arrivals measure inbound flows.

questions.stem: A hotel has 80 rooms and sold 1,920 room-nights in a 30-day month. Its room occupancy rate for the month is
questions.explanation: Available room-nights = 80 x 30 = 2,400; 1,920 / 2,400 = 80%.

questions.stem: Which of these is an economic benefit of tourism to a nation?
options: Erosion of local culture through copying foreign ways
questions.explanation: Foreign tourists spend foreign currency.

questions.stem: Tourism promotes understanding between peoples of different backgrounds. This is a
questions.explanation: Cultural exchange is a social benefit.

questions.topic: Festivals and Heritages in a Nation
questions.stem: Fishermen dive into the Matan Fada river with nets and gourds at a famous annual festival. In which state does this take place?
questions.explanation: Argungu is in Kebbi State.

questions.topic: Festivals and Heritages in a Nation
questions.stem: The Osun-Osogbo Sacred Grove in Osun State is significant because it is
options: the site of Nigeria's first airport
the headquarters of a travel agency
questions.explanation: The Grove was inscribed as a World Heritage Site in 2005.

questions.stem: A businesswoman flies from Lagos to Accra to attend a trade fair. Her reason for travel is mainly
questions.explanation: Trade fairs and business meetings are economic reasons.

questions.stem: Pilgrimages to Mecca or Jerusalem are examples of travel for
questions.explanation: Pilgrimage is religious travel.

questions.stem: Booking flights and issuing tickets for customers are functions of a
questions.explanation: Travel agents handle reservations and ticketing.

questions.stem: A travel agent earns income mainly from
options: commission paid by airlines, hotels and tour operators
salaries paid by government to all registered travel agents
questions.explanation: Agents earn commission from principals.

questions.stem: A business that combines transport, accommodation and sightseeing into one package and sells it at an inclusive price is a
questions.explanation: Tour operators assemble package tours.

questions.stem: Which of these is the correct sequence of a tour operator's main roles?
options: Executing the tour first, then packaging it, and marketing it at the very end
Marketing the tour, executing it, then packaging it
Packaging the tour, marketing it, then executing (operating) it
Packaging, executing, then marketing after the tour ends
Executing, marketing, then packaging the next year
questions.explanation: Tour operators package, market and then execute tours.

questions.stem: A bureau de change supports tourism by
options: guiding visitors around museums and monuments
questions.explanation: Bureaux de change provide currency exchange.

questions.stem: Insurance companies support the travel business mainly by
options: providing travel insurance against risks such as illness and lost luggage
issuing visas and passports to travellers going abroad on holiday
questions.explanation: Travel insurance covers trip risks.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a public agency involved in tourism in Nigeria?
options: The Federation of Tourism Associations of Nigeria
The National Association of Nigerian Travel Agencies
questions.explanation: State tourism boards are government agencies.

questions.stem: A major role of public tourism agencies in Nigeria is to
options: formulate policy, regulate standards and promote the country as a destination
operate private hotels and resorts for the benefit of their own members and staff
questions.explanation: Public agencies make policy, regulate and promote.

questions.stem: NANTA, a private agency in tourism, is the association of
questions.explanation: NANTA is the National Association of Nigerian Travel Agencies.

questions.stem: Hoteliers, travel agents and tour operators each have their own associations, and these associations are in turn federated under one body called
questions.explanation: FTAN is the Federation of Tourism Associations of Nigeria.

questions.stem: Promoting a destination to all kinds of visitors with one general message is
questions.explanation: Mass marketing targets the whole market.

questions.stem: A resort that designs special packages only for bird-watchers is practising
questions.explanation: Niche marketing targets a narrow segment.

questions.stem: Making and selling tie-and-dye fabrics to visitors is an example of a
questions.explanation: Small home-based crafts are cottage industries.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a tourism-related business opportunity for a young entrepreneur?
options: Manufacturing aircraft engines for airlines operating in West Africa
Running a small guest house near a tourist site
questions.explanation: Small guest houses serve tourists with modest capital.

questions.stem: A person who accompanies tourists and explains the history of the sites they visit is a
questions.explanation: Tour guides interpret sites for visitors.

questions.stem: Which of the following best describes good service delivery in tourism?
options: Charging tourists the highest possible price for every service they request
Meeting or exceeding visitors' expectations with courtesy and efficiency
Keeping visitors waiting for long periods
Providing services only to foreign tourists
questions.explanation: Good service satisfies visitors consistently.

questions.stem: NIHOTOUR is a government institution that
options: trains people in hospitality and tourism skills
issues international passports to Nigerian citizens
questions.explanation: The National Institute for Hospitality and Tourism trains workers.

questions.stem: Which agency supports small and medium enterprises, including craft businesses that serve tourists, with training and advice?
questions.explanation: SMEDAN develops small and medium enterprises.

questions.stem:
(a) Define the tourist product. [2 marks]
(b) State two characteristics of the tourist product. [2 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: the total experience offered to a tourist, combining attractions, accessibility, accommodation and services
1 mark: intangible
1 mark: perishable / heterogeneous / immovable / inseparable
questions.explanation: The tourist product is the combined experience of attractions, transport, accommodation and services a visitor buys. It is intangible, perishable, heterogeneous, immovable and produced and consumed at the same time.

questions.topic: Festivals and Heritages in a Nation
questions.stem:
(a) Name two festivals in Nigeria and the state where each is held. [2 marks]
(b) Name two World Heritage Sites in Nigeria. [2 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
1 mark: Argungu Fishing Festival, Kebbi State
1 mark: Osun-Osogbo Festival, Osun State / Calabar Carnival, Cross River / Eyo Festival, Lagos / Durbar, Kano
1 mark: Osun-Osogbo Sacred Grove
1 mark: Sukur Cultural Landscape
questions.explanation: Examples: Argungu Fishing Festival (Kebbi), Osun-Osogbo Festival (Osun), Calabar Carnival (Cross River), Eyo (Lagos), Durbar (Kano/Katsina). Nigeria's UNESCO World Heritage Sites are the Sukur Cultural Landscape (Adamawa) and the Osun-Osogbo Sacred Grove (Osun).

questions.stem:
(a) Distinguish between natural and man-made tourist attractions. [4 marks]
(b) Name four natural tourist attractions in Nigeria and state where each is located. [8 marks]
(c) Explain four problems that hinder the development of tourist attractions in Nigeria. [8 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: natural attractions are features of nature such as hills, waterfalls, beaches and wildlife
2 marks: man-made attractions are created by people, such as museums, monuments and palaces
2 marks: Yankari Game Reserve, Bauchi State
2 marks: Obudu Mountain Resort (plateau), Cross River State
2 marks: Ikogosi Warm Springs, Ekiti State
2 marks: Olumo Rock (Ogun) / Erin Ijesha Waterfalls (Osun) / Kainji Lake National Park / Bar Beach (Lagos)
2 marks: poor roads and infrastructure
2 marks: insecurity
2 marks: inadequate funding and maintenance
2 marks: poor publicity / inadequate accommodation and amenities / lack of skilled personnel
questions.explanation: Natural attractions are nature's features; man-made ones are built by people. Examples: Yankari (Bauchi), Obudu (Cross River), Ikogosi (Ekiti), Olumo Rock (Ogun), Erin Ijesha Waterfalls (Osun). Problems include poor infrastructure, insecurity, under-funding and poor maintenance, weak publicity, inadequate amenities and lack of trained staff.

questions.stem:
(a) Explain five economic benefits of tourism to Nigeria. [10 marks]
(b) Explain five negative effects of tourism on a host community. [10 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: earns foreign exchange
2 marks: creates employment in hotels, transport, crafts and guiding
2 marks: generates government revenue through taxes and levies
2 marks: stimulates development of infrastructure
2 marks: promotes local industries such as crafts / improves balance of payments
2 marks: erosion or commercialisation of local culture
2 marks: environmental damage such as pollution and littering
2 marks: rise in prices of goods and land (inflation)
2 marks: increase in crime, drug abuse or immoral behaviour
2 marks: congestion / seasonal unemployment / leakage of earnings to foreign firms
questions.explanation: Tourism earns foreign exchange, creates jobs, yields taxes and levies, drives infrastructure and boosts local industries and the balance of payments. It can also erode culture, damage the environment, raise local prices, increase crime and congestion, create seasonal jobs and let profits leak abroad.

questions.stem:
(a) Who is a travel agent? [2 marks]
(b) Explain five functions of a travel agent. [10 marks]
(c) State four qualities of a good travel agent. [8 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: a person or firm that sells travel products such as tickets, accommodation and tours on behalf of principals for commission
2 marks: reservation of flights, hotels and car hire
2 marks: ticketing
2 marks: assisting with visa procurement and travel documents
2 marks: arranging foreign exchange and travel insurance
2 marks: giving travel information and advice / selling package tours
2 marks: honesty and integrity
2 marks: good communication and customer service skills
2 marks: good knowledge of destinations and travel regulations
2 marks: computer (reservation system) skills / patience / good public relations
questions.explanation: A travel agent sells travel services for principals and earns commission. Functions: reservations, ticketing, visa assistance, foreign exchange and insurance arrangements, information and package sales. Qualities: honesty, communication and customer care, destination knowledge, computer skills and patience.

questions.stem:
(a) Explain the meaning of service delivery in tourism. [2 marks]
(b) Explain the roles of each of the following in service delivery: (i) tour guide; (ii) receptionist; (iii) game guard; (iv) cultural dancer. [12 marks]
(c) State three ways of improving service delivery in the Nigerian tourism industry. [6 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: the way services are provided to tourists so that their needs and expectations are met satisfactorily
3 marks: tour guide: leads visitors, interprets history and culture of sites and ensures their safety
3 marks: receptionist: welcomes guests, handles check-in, reservations and enquiries
3 marks: game guard: protects wildlife and visitors in parks and guides game viewing
3 marks: cultural dancer: entertains visitors and showcases local culture
2 marks: training and retraining of staff
2 marks: improving infrastructure and facilities
2 marks: setting and enforcing service standards / rewarding good service / handling complaints promptly
questions.explanation: Service delivery is how services are provided to satisfy tourists. Tour guides lead and interpret; receptionists welcome and register guests; game guards protect wildlife and visitors; cultural dancers entertain and display culture. Improve delivery through training, better facilities, enforced standards, incentives and prompt complaint handling.
